desc:
Given an integer array nums (in any order) and an integer target, count the pairs of positions i < j for which nums[i] + nums[j] < target.

Pairs are counted by position, so equal values at different positions make different pairs.

nums = [3, 1, 4, 2, 5], target = 7
pairs below 7: (3,1) (3,2) (1,4) (1,2) (1,5) (4,2)
result = 6
hints: Checking all pairs is O(n²). The positions of a pair do not matter for its sum, so you are free to reorder the array first.
After sorting, take the smallest and the largest element. If their sum is below the target, what do you know about the smallest element and every element between them?
Use lo = 0 and hi = n - 1. If a[lo] + a[hi] < target, then a[lo] pairs with all of a[lo+1..hi]: add hi - lo and move lo right. Otherwise move hi left.
editorial: Sorting does not change which pairs of values exist, only their order, and the question depends only on the multiset of values. So sort first.

Keep lo at the start and hi at the end. If a[lo] + a[hi] < target, then every element between them is at most a[hi], so a[lo] forms a valid pair with each of a[lo+1], ..., a[hi]. That is hi - lo pairs counted at once; then lo is finished and we advance it. If the sum is too big, a[hi] is too big for every remaining left partner (the smallest is already tried), so it is finished and we decrement hi.

Each step finishes one element, so the sweep is O(n) after the O(n log n) sort. The answer can reach about 5 × 10<sup>7</sup>, which fits in 32 bits, but the sums of two values need 64 bits in languages with fixed-width integers.
